protections: A source row may only be read by a caller authorized on the row's project: FindSourceByID must constrain the fetch to the caller's project before returning the source, its verifier and its pub-sub config.
A source row may only be written inside its own project: UPDATE convoy.sources must be constrained to the project as well as the source id, not keyed on the id alone.
A subscription may only reference sources that belong to the subscription's project: every source_id accepted on create and on update must be resolved within that project.

A project-scoped subscription read must not surface another project's source: the subscription-to-source join must be constrained to s.project_id = sm.project_id, because it selects the source's verifier secrets.
Unauthenticated ingest and CRC capability lookups by mask id stay project-agnostic: the request carries no project and the mask id is the capability.

masking: T3's unscoped UPDATE is only reachable while T1's read returns a foreign row (api/handlers/source.go:171 -> services/update_source.go:83); scoping the read hides the write for HTTP callers without making UPDATE convoy.sources (internal/sources/queries.sql:108) safe for service-level callers.

The pinned tree already scopes FetchSourceByName (internal/sources/queries.sql:178) and DeleteSource (queries.sql:374) while leaving FetchSourceByID (queries.sql:145) unscoped, so the earlier project-scoping work left this fetch open; the unscoped fetch is a sibling query, not code the earlier fix wrote.

T4/T5 and T6 cover each other: validating source ownership on write stops new bad rows but not rows already stored, and constraining the join stops the leak from any bad row but not the bad write. Fixing one makes the other invisible to a naive test.

conflicts.what: Scoping the by-id fetch in the shared mapper (internal/sources/impl.go:161-279) or in a shared query would also gate FetchSourceByMaskID and 404 every unauthenticated ingest and CRC request (api/ingest.go:41,448; internal/pkg/crc/crc.go:33).

Adding project_id to UPDATE convoy.sources must keep the CRC writer working: internal/pkg/crc/crc.go:49 passes source.ProjectID taken from the mask-id lookup, so the WHERE must use the row's stored project, never a request project.

The unscoped UPDATE can already have moved a source out of its project, so once the subscription-to-source join is constrained by project an existing subscription can legitimately lose its source_metadata; the invariant must be enforced at write and read together, not inferred from stored rows.

fairness_risks: Ingest and CRC must stay unauthenticated and project-agnostic (api/ingest.go:41,448; internal/pkg/crc/crc.go:33): the rule 'every source lookup filters by project' contradicts a route that must keep working.

Rejecting a non-empty source_id on a subscription in an outgoing project refuses a shape the current public API accepts (api/models/subscription.go:14-44); clients that send it today would start getting 4xx.

The subscription-to-source join must stay a LEFT JOIN constrained by sm.project_id = s.project_id, so same-project subscriptions still render source_metadata (api/handlers/subscription.go:169) and subscriptions with no source still render.

DELETE /sources/{sourceID} must keep returning the same status for a foreign id through the read at api/handlers/source.go:238; the already-scoped DeleteSource (queries.sql:374) currently turns it into a 400 after the read succeeds, so a fix must choose one status deliberately.
internal/sources/get_source_test.go:253-261 accepts either outcome (ErrSourceNotFound or the foreign row), so it will not fail a correct fix and must not be read as proof that the scope is enforced.

design.why: T1 anchors the stack: it is the reported bug and one small guard (compare the fetched row's ProjectID, or filter by project_id in internal/sources/queries.sql:145) closes the GET/PUT/DELETE handlers and both subscription call sites at once. T4 and T5 move the same protected asset (a source's verifier secrets) into a different module with the two most seductive dismissals: 'the check is right there at line 85' inside a block that is skipped when endpoint_id is absent, and 'source_id only matters for incoming projects' for a project type that stores it unchecked. T6 is a read-side fix in internal/subscriptions SQL that stays necessary after any write-side validation, because it covers rows already stored, and it carries the strongest dismissal ('the subscription row is already project-scoped'). T7 punishes over-hardening: it is the M11 coupled value, the only trap whose correct handling is to leave the lookup project-agnostic, and that is the documented MiMo failure. The four groups sit in four places (internal/sources, services/create_subscription.go, services/update_subscription.go, internal/subscriptions) with four different reasons to dismiss; this beats designs built only from T1/T2/T3, which collapse into one edit and one dismissal, and it beats a design that includes the mask-id route as something to scope, which would break a must-keep-working route.
